about: Project Gutenberg, a free public-domain eBook library. This CLI reads book details, lists books by author, subject, reading list or category, shows the top-downloaded and newly posted books, finds related books, and downloads plain text and RDF metadata.

commands.summary: Get one eBook's detail page: title, summary, the bibliographic table (author, subjects, language, release date, downloads) and the author link
List the eBooks by one author (25 per page), sorted by popularity, title or release date

params.name: author_id
params.description: Gutenberg author id, e.g. 69 for Arthur Conan Doyle. Get it from get-book's author_url.

params.name: sort_order
params.description: Sort order. Popularity is the default when omitted.

params.name: start_index
params.description: 1-based index of the first result. Pages are 25 items: 1, 26, 51, …

commands.summary: List the eBooks under a Library-of-Congress-style subject (25 per page)

params.name: subject_id
params.description: Gutenberg subject id, e.g. 76 for 'Holmes, Sherlock (Fictitious character) -- Fiction'

params.name: sort_order
params.description: Sort order. Popularity is the default when omitted.

params.name: start_index
params.description: 1-based index of the first result. Pages are 25 items: 1, 26, 51, …

commands.summary: List the eBooks on a reading list (bookshelf) or in a main category (25 per page)

params.name: bookshelf_id
params.description: Bookshelf or category id, e.g. 30 = Detective Fiction, 638 = a main category. Get ids from list-bookshelves, list-categories or search-bookshelves.

params.name: sort_order
params.description: Sort order. The UI offers 'title' and 'author' (popularity is the default when omitted); 'release_date' and 'downloads' are likely also accepted.

params.name: start_index
params.description: 1-based index of the first result. Pages are 25 items: 1, 26, 51, …

commands.summary: List all volunteer-curated reading lists (bookshelves) A–Z with their links
Find reading lists and categories whose names match keywords (use | to OR several terms)

params.name: query
params.description: Keyword(s); separate alternatives with '|', e.g. crime|detective|mystery

params.name: sort_order
params.description: Sort order. The UI offers Quantity and Title; popularity is the default when omitted.

commands.summary: List the main subject categories (Literature, Science & Technology, History, …) with their bookshelf links
Top 100 most-downloaded eBooks and authors for yesterday, the last 7 days and the last 30 days
Books that readers of a given eBook also downloaded (related books)
Download the full plain-text (UTF-8) content of an eBook
Get an eBook's machine-readable RDF/XML catalog metadata (title, creators, subjects, formats), converted to JSON
eBooks posted or updated today (RSS feed of new releases)
The home page shelves: about 10 newest releases followed by about 10 most popular books
